slides.title: RoboGesture: Real-Time Semantic-aligned Co-Speech Gestures Generation for Humanoid Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME CO-SPEECH GESTURE GENERATION FOR HUMANOIDS
slides.highlight: RoboGesture introduces a framework for generating synchronized, semantically meaningful gestures in real time, supporting the development of natural human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: RoboGesture enables humanoid robots to generate real-time, semantically aligned, and collision-free co-speech gestures from audio.
card.key_idea: A framework using a hierarchical semantic-acoustic aligner and a diffusion transformer with anti-inertia CFG masking, supported by a semi-synthetic dataset and an MPC-based safety filter.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on BEAT and SemanticBEAT datasets using FGD, BC, and human studies; outperformed baselines in semantic accuracy and physical consistency.

slides.title: Synthetic Linguistic Agency: How an Embodied Mortal Agent Learns Linguistic Affordances through Consequential Social Experience
slides.tldr: EMBODIED MORTAL AGENT LEARNS LINGUISTIC AGENCY
slides.highlight: This work introduces an Embodied Mortal Agent (EMA) that learns how linguistic choices affect a partner's willingness to protect its life, providing insights into embodied social robots and human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: Introduces Synthetic Linguistic Agency (SLA) and an Embodied Mortal Agent that learns language through survival.
card.key_idea: MGL-RL connects linguistic affordances to a 'mortal body' where strategic speech acts (appeals/exchanges) regulate the agent's remaining useful life (Reference-RUL) based on social history.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via controlled experiments and counterfactuals on an EMA cohort, testing if linguistic choices depend on body state, social history, and partner behavior.
card.limitation: The agent's linguistic capacity is limited to a fixed action repertoire rendered into text, rather than open-ended generation.

slides.title: RegulAR: Graph-Grounded Error Recognition and Assistance for Procedural Tasks in AR
slides.tldr: AR ASSISTANT FOR PROCEDURAL ERROR RECOVERY
slides.highlight: RegulAR uses a hierarchical dependency graph and MLLM to identify procedural deviations and provide recovery guidance, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on adaptive AI coaching for human skill improvement.

card.one_liner: RegulAR is an AR assistant that uses task dependency graphs and MLLMs to proactively support procedural error recovery.
card.key_idea: It converts instructions into a hierarchical dependency graph, combining it with MLLM-based egocentric observation to track progress, categorize errors, and estimate downstream impact for adaptive guidance.
card.evaluation: A within-subject study (N=12) compared RegulAR to an MLLM-only baseline; participants reported better task-structure understanding and recovery support with RegulAR.
card.limitation: The system surfaces trade-offs between the timing of interventions and the preservation of user autonomy.

slides.title: A Conceptual Framework for Modeling Team Adaptation in Cooperative Games Through Ludic Knowledge
slides.tldr: FRAMEWORK FOR TEAM ADAPTATION IN COOPERATIVE GAMES
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a framework for analyzing team adaptability in cooperative games, specifically utilizing Overcooked! to examine how game design triggers adaptive behaviors. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that adapt during human-AI teaming in Overcooked-AI.

card.one_liner: A framework for analyzing team adaptability in cooperative games based on the activation or disruption of ludic knowledge.
card.key_idea: Adaptive stimuli are categorized as retrieval-based (explicit signals) or disruption-based (novelty or discrepancy), which either activate existing ludic knowledge or force the construction of new schemata.
card.evaluation: Qualitative interaction analysis of a single team playing Overcooked! using gameplay videos. Results are illustrative but limited by a small sample size.
card.limitation: Small sample size and use of found footage, which limits access to players' internal expectations and mental models.

slides.title: How Much Can AI Understand? Toward AI-Assisted Sensemaking of Collaborative Discussion in Groups with Shared History
slides.tldr: AI-ASSISTED SENSEMAKING FOR GROUP DISCUSSIONS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a model for AI-assisted sensemaking that captures group norms and participant context, aligning with HyECHO's focus on social perception and group norms in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Proposed AI model for sensemaking in collaborative discussions by integrating social context and shared group history.
card.key_idea: An AI-assisted sensemaking model that overlays extraction, prioritization, connecting, and presentation onto human cognitive processes, incorporating arguments, community norms, and participant contexts.
card.evaluation: Based on two studies of experienced Wikipedia editors' cognitive processes and a web-based LLM-assisted prototype; results are not quantitatively detailed.
card.limitation: High system interpretive work risks dehumanizing participants, erasing minority opinions, and creating false consensus if the AI lacks social intelligibility.

slides.title: Augmenting Human Performance with an XR Agent Learning from Online Behavior and BCI Evidence
slides.tldr: XR AGENT ADAPTING TO BEHAVIORAL AND PHYSIOLOGICAL SIGNALS
slides.highlight: The OLIVE framework enables an XR agent to adapt in real-time by fusing behavioral and EEG signals to infer task relevance, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that adapt at test time and infer partner intent.

card.one_liner: OLIVE augments human performance in XR by fusing behavioral and EEG evidence to adapt a VLM.
card.key_idea: An online EM loop jointly estimates source reliability and tunes a frozen VLM's virtual prompt using explicit actions and implicit fixation-locked EEG signals.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via three user studies in an XR game; OLIVE-IE achieved 96.8% guidance convergence in 28.3s, Pareto-dominating single-modality variants and TPT/TDA baselines.

slides.title: Faireez offers housekeeping services to collect data for robot training
slides.tldr: DATA COLLECTION FOR ROBOT TRAINING
slides.highlight: Faireez is collecting data through housekeeping services to train humanoid robots, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied AI and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: A Human-AI Theorem Connecting Spontaneous and Field-Induced Mechanisms of Collective Behavior in One Dimension
slides.tldr: HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION DISCOVERS STATISTICAL PHYSICS THEOREM
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how sustained human-AI collaboration can generate scientific breakthroughs in statistical physics, supporting MIMIC's focus on modeling human-AI societies and agent-based interactions.

card.one_liner: A human-AI collaboration proves a theorem mapping range-two 1D spin chains to simpler range-one chains.
card.key_idea: A recursive Householder moving-frame transformation provides a temperature-independent Hamiltonian-level mapping for O(n) and q-state Potts open chains with arbitrary inhomogeneous interactions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via geometric proofs and linear specialization to known models (Ising, XY, Heisenberg); results provide closed-form solutions for the J1-J2 Potts chain.
card.limitation: The proven Hamiltonian-level mapping is specifically restricted to open boundary conditions (OBC) rather than periodic chains.

slides.title: TEIDAN: A Multilingual Multiparty Dialogue Corpus
slides.tldr: MULTILINGUAL MULTIPARTY DIALOGUE CORPUS
slides.highlight: This corpus of spontaneous face-to-face triadic discussions supports research on addressee recognition and turn-taking, contributing to the multimodal social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: TEIDAN is a multilingual multimodal corpus of spontaneous three-party face-to-face discussions in Japanese and English.
card.key_idea: The corpus uses pin microphones, microphone arrays, and cameras to record triadic interactions, providing IPU-based transcripts for cross-linguistic analysis of turn-taking and multimodal grounding.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via descriptive quantitative statistics and qualitative sequential analysis of 69 sessions; results show distinct turn-organization differences between English and Japanese.
card.limitation: Differences in participant relationships (acquainted Japanese speakers vs. stranger English speakers) may confound cross-linguistic and cultural comparisons.

slides.title: When Robots Mishear Us: Mapping the Safety Risks of Voice-Controlled Embodied AI
slides.tldr: ASR ERRORS INCREASE EMBODIED AI SAFETY RISKS
slides.highlight: This research examines how automatic speech recognition errors can lead embodied AI to execute harmful instructions, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: ASR errors in voice-controlled embodied AI can bypass safety filters and trigger unsafe physical actions.
card.key_idea: A framework simulating five ASR error types (e.g., acoustic substitution, noise) was used to test if corrupted instructions weaken model refusal and planning robustness.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using POEX and SafeAgentBench with Qwen2.5-7B, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4.1-mini. Results show increased acceptance rates for harmful tasks under specific errors.
card.limitation: Automatic ASR correction is not always effective, particularly when input semantics are heavily damaged by severe noise.

slides.title: In-Context Neurofeedback: Can LLMs Control Their Internal Representations through Privileged Access?
slides.tldr: LLMS STRUGGLE TO CONTROL PRIVILEGED INTERNAL REPRESENTATIONS
slides.highlight: This research examines whether LLMs can control internal representations via neurofeedback, providing insights into the requirements for rigorous assessment of machine metacognition relevant to ADAM-CHAT.

card.one_liner: LLMs fail to reliably control privileged internal representations when surface-level textual cues are removed.
card.key_idea: In-Context Neurofeedback (ICN) requires models to maximize a probe-based score while outputting a fixed sentence, ensuring control targets are privileged and not inferable from text.
card.evaluation: Tested four open-weight models (Llama-3.1, Qwen3) across three datasets (SST, ETHICS, True-False). Results showed inconsistent significance and small effect sizes (d < 0.5).
card.limitation: Findings are limited to the specific models, datasets, and features (sentiment, ethics, truthfulness) tested.

slides.title: Mind the Gap: Theory-of-Mind-Grounded Friction for Epistemic Alignment
slides.tldr: THEORY-OF-MIND GROUNDED FRICTION FOR EPISTEMIC ALIGNMENT
slides.highlight: This work proposes a Theory-of-Mind (ToM) inference framework to detect silent divergence in belief states between participants. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: ToM-grounded friction improves LLM intervention and calibration in collaborative dialogues by modeling higher-order belief divergence.
card.key_idea: Uses a four-part Theory-of-Mind schema (speaker/addressee beliefs and their models of each other) to compute a deterministic friction signal for policy optimization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HCRC MapTask using intervention F1, ECE, and Brier scores; FAR and FTR variants outperformed DPO in stability and calibration.
card.limitation: High intervention F1 in some baselines suggests the model preserves existing competence rather than learning new capabilities from scratch.

slides.title: AI as Teammate: Rethinking Task Distribution in Medical Training
slides.tldr: METACOGNITIVE FRAMEWORK FOR AI TASK ALLOCATION
slides.highlight: This paper proposes the SCAN framework to address AI misclassification in medical training through real-time metacognitive evaluation, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and adaptive human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Reframes AI misuse in medical training as a 'misclassification' of task allocation based on learner competence.
card.key_idea: The SCAN framework (Substitute, Complement, Aid, Non-Negotiable) uses Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development to align AI interaction modes with a learner's metacognitive needs.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper proposes a conceptual framework and a testable research agenda rather than empirical results.
card.limitation: Passive engagement in correctly classified tasks can lead to 'mis-skilling,' requiring human experts to act as epistemic auditors.

slides.title: SocialReasonBench: A Video-QA Benchmark for Social Reasoning with Counterfactual Narrative Videos
slides.tldr: VIDEO-QA BENCHMARK FOR SOCIAL REASONING
slides.highlight: This benchmark evaluates the ability of Large Multimodal Models to reason about human-centered social dynamics and counterfactuals, supporting MIMIC's focus on modeling agent behavior in hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: SocialReasonBench evaluates LMMs' social reasoning using counterfactual scenarios derived from branching narrative gameplay videos.
card.key_idea: A multi-agent pipeline extracts clips from Detroit: Become Human, grounding QA pairs in game-state signals across seven dimensions, including counterfactual and causal reasoning.
card.evaluation: Eight LMMs were tested on 532 QA pairs. Results show models handle basic social understanding but struggle with causal and counterfactual reasoning.
card.limitation: The benchmark relies on a single English-language game, potentially reflecting specific cultural/narrative styles and introducing generator-family bias via Gemini-based curation.

slides.title: Social bots weaken activist cohesion
slides.tldr: BOTS ERODE HUMAN NETWORK COHESION
slides.highlight: This research examines how bot exposure dissolves human ties and weakens collective action, providing insights into the social perception of group cohesion relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Social bot exposure during protest peaks erodes the human network cohesion necessary to sustain collective action.
card.key_idea: Analyzed 2020 BLM retweet networks to show bot interaction predicts subsequent declines in human triadic closure (ego-networks) and edge density (communities), especially among movement supporters.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using longitudinal Twitter data (pre, during, and post-peak) with OLS regressions and GPT-3.5 stance classification; results were robust across bot-probability thresholds.

slides.title: Behavior--Realization Separation for Constrained Physical Human--Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: SEPARATING BEHAVIOR SPECIFICATION FROM CONSTRAINED REALIZATION
slides.highlight: This work proposes a layered architecture for physical human-robot interaction that separates desired behavior from constrained realization, improving boundary precision and torque feasibility. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposes a software architecture separating desired interaction behavior from its constrained physical robot realization.
card.key_idea: A behavior layer specifies desired acceleration; a predictive QP realization layer converts this into feasible commands and audits residuals to distinguish constraint intervention from model error.
card.evaluation: Simulated on a planar point mass and 7-DOF Franka FR3 in MuJoCo; compared against reactive clipping using RMSE and overshoot metrics.
card.limitation: The predictive QP implementation is validated only for memoryless affine behaviors; nonlinear or stateful specifications may require different machinery.

slides.title: Quiq Launches Voice Assist
slides.tldr: AGENTIC AI FOR LIVE CALLS
slides.highlight: The launch of Voice Assist introduces agentic AI capable of acting during live calls, which relates to ADAM-CHAT's focus on adaptive agents for human-AI teaming.

slides.title: Hark Partners with NVIDIA to Advance Personalized Agentic AI
slides.tldr: PERSONALIZED AGENTIC AI ADVANCEMENT
slides.highlight: Hark's focus on personalized agentic AI aligns with ADAM-CHAT's goals of developing adaptive AI teammates.

slides.title: FIS-OT: Feature-Induced Optimal Transport for Unsupervised Action Segmentation
slides.tldr: UNSUPERVISED ACTION SEGMENTATION VIA FEATURE-INDUCED OPTIMAL TRANSPORT
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Feature-Induced Structured Optimal Transport framework to improve action segmentation by aligning local feature learning with global structural alignment, supporting the MOSAIC goal of using Optimal Transport for intent alignment.

card.one_liner: FIS-OT improves unsupervised action segmentation by linking local feature learning with global structural optimal transport.
card.key_idea: Combines a Feature Enhanced Generator using triplet loss for local consistency with a dynamic, feature-induced residual structural prior for global Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport alignment.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Breakfast, 50Salads, and Desktop Assembly datasets using MoF, F1, and mIoU; outperformed ASOT, especially in short-action detection.
card.limitation: Sensitivity to noise within individual videos, as global matching in Optimal Transport can be affected by severe occlusions.

slides.title: Between Algorithm (AI) and Intuition (Human): Preserving Designer Agency in AI-Assisted Sensemaking of Qualitative UX Data
slides.tldr: AI-ASSISTED QUALITATIVE SENSEMAKING
slides.highlight: This work explores the tension between algorithmic efficiency and human intuition in qualitative data analysis, offering a framework for augmented sensemaking. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on the hybrid state of human-AI teams and the preservation of human judgment.

card.one_liner: A framework for AI-assisted qualitative UX research that preserves human interpretive agency over mechanical sorting.
card.key_idea: Positions AI as an instrument to amplify human judgment and intentional subjectivity rather than replacing the designer's intuitive sensemaking process.
card.evaluation: Case study analyzing 20 user responses on educational video conferencing via comparative analysis of AI-assisted versus human-centered approaches.
card.limitation: AI tools risk flattening rich data patterns and transforming interpretive design research into a sterile, mechanical sorting exercise.

slides.title: Cooperative Risk-Aware Exploration in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems Using Algorithmic Altruism
slides.tldr: ALTRUISTIC RISK-AWARE EXPLORATION
slides.highlight: This work proposes a game-theoretic framework for heterogeneous multi-robot exploration that uses altruistic coupling to distribute risk and reduce redundancy. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on understanding team states and coordination within hybrid human-AI systems.

card.one_liner: A game-theoretic framework for multi-robot exploration where low-value robots altruistically accept higher risks for the team.
card.key_idea: Uses Hamilton's rule to shape utilities via value-based relatedness weights, inducing a weighted potential game that converges to Pareto-optimal trajectories through decentralized fictitious play.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulations and hardware experiments with wheeled robots; results showed reduced redundancy, improved robot separation, and risk reallocation while maintaining map coverage.
card.limitation: Theoretical guarantees of global optimality and Pareto-optimality require the weighted potential function to be strictly jointly concave.

slides.title: R³: Training Robots to Reason in Natural Language via Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: NATURAL LANGUAGE REASONING FOR ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work explores using free-form language reasoning as a test-time compute mechanism to guide low-level policies, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that adapt at test time and self-monitor to handle long-horizon tasks.

card.one_liner: $\mathcal{R}^3$ trains VLMs to use free-form natural language reasoning to steer low-level robotic manipulation policies.
card.key_idea: A two-stage recipe: mid-training on expert reasoning traces to initialize style, followed by single-step rubric-based RL using offline instruction-only data to optimize reasoning for action.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Language Table and simulated grocery packing; outperformed instruction-only imitation learning, especially on out-of-distribution tasks, using success rates as the primary metric.
card.limitation: Performance can degrade on tasks with substantial behavioral gaps between the base model and the expert, such as 'diag_line'.
